commits.message: fix(lint): each extension set has one spelling, the page script reads only the browser, and a loader the zone rule cannot follow is refused (candybar-later-fixes-nwu9.1d4)

fix(lint): what a loader loads is judged as an import is, and every file of a root outside Jest is type-checked (candybar-later-fixes-nwu9.1d4)

The zone rule's edge reader follows each loader Node hands code (require,
module.require, process.getBuiltinModule, and the loader createRequire
makes, under any name it is bound to) and judges each call's source; any
other use of a loader is refused, and a relative source on a base no lint
can read is refused. The owner list for node:module is gone.

tsconfig.json includes each root whole, so no extension is spelled there,
and the type-environment test places a probe of each TypeScript extension
in every root by the project's own include and checks it in a program over
the project's every file.

The lockfile is pnpm 10's, as CI installs it.

fix(lint): code outside Jest runs in a closed environment, and the zone rule reads every edge a Jest package arrives by (candybar-later-fixes-nwu9.1d4)

Review pass 2 of #952: the refusal leaned on hand-kept lists of Jest's
names, which missed real ones (`fail`, `pending`, `babel-jest`) and which
the tests were generated from.

- Globals: the app's and the tools' environments are closed. TypeScript is
  type-checked with Node's types alone; src's and the tools' JavaScript read
  only Node's globals (and the browser's, for the bar-web page) under
  `no-undef` with `typeof`. The deny list and its copy of Jest's globals are
  gone; the test roots declare `globals`' Jest set and the fixture hook.
- Packages: Jest's are every package named for it, a `jest` word in its
  scope or name, and `expect`. One zone table judges paths and packages
  through one `mayImport`, and a row or package naming no zone fails the
  table's load.
- Edges: the zone rule reads `module.require` and triple-slash references,
  and src's `.js` is linted. `node:module`, whose `createRequire` loads what
  no lint can place, is imported only by its named owners.
- One extension set spells every glob and every stripped key.
- Tests take Jest's names from a list written out by hand, so a name the
  rules miss fails a case; a type-check of a probe under each tsconfig
  proves the app project refuses Jest's globals and the test project knows
  them.

fix(types): the app's type environment holds none of Jest's, and src's own lint refuses Jest's globals and packages (candybar-later-fixes-nwu9.1d4)

Review pass 1 of #952: the cause was one TypeScript project holding src and
the tests, and src's lint config declaring Jest's globals legal.

- tsconfig.json is the app's project with Node's types alone; test/tsconfig.json
  extends it with Jest's for test/ and audits/. A Jest global in app code,
  `globalThis.jest` included, is a type error. `typecheck` checks both.
- src's lint no longer declares Jest's globals; the test roots' block does,
  for an editor linting a test. src refuses each as undefined.
- Packages have zone rows: Jest's (jest, jest-*, @jest/*, expect, ts-jest,
  @types/jest) are the test zone's, judged by the one mayImport and REFUSAL
  as a path is, in src's .js files too. The tools config's own package
  pattern, which missed require, is gone.
- Jest's globals are listed once, in the zone table, and the tools config,
  the test roots' globals and the tests all read that list.
- The second lint of src through the tools config is reverted.

fix(lint): code outside Jest, src included, imports none of Jest's packages and reads none of its globals (candybar-later-fixes-nwu9.1d4)

src could import @jest/globals, jest-mock or expect, or call a Jest global,
and pass both lint and typecheck: the Jest refusal covered only the tool roots,
and test/ shares src's tsconfig, so Jest's global types reach src.

- Jest's packages are the test zone's in the zone map, so the one zone rule
  refuses them in every spelling of an edge (import, require, import(), type
  import) from every zone but test: src through its config, the tools through
  theirs. The separate no-restricted-imports pattern, which missed require,
  is gone.
- The roots the Jest-globals refusal covers are derived from the zone map:
  every top-level directory a row outside the test zone lies in, src among them.
- The lint-rule tests prove both for every root outside Jest.
fix(limits): each process's charge is asked of it, a gap carries, and rotation keeps the host's apart from one renderer pool (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.8xv)
fix(renderer): an end is one owned transition, and a stats reply is read against every arm (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.8xv)
test(stats): an unread renderer's fixture carries the gap its charge holds (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.8xv)

fix(host): every spawned renderer is judged from its spawn on its own reading, and each process's breaches rotate apart (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.8xv)

- A renderer enters every reading from its spawn. One no ping has read yet
  is charged by the platform, and one nothing could charge is unread,
  logged as such and never judged, so it is told apart from a renderer
  that is down.
- A reading is keyed by its spawn (name and generation), so a later spawn
  given an earlier one's pid inherits neither its reading nor its gap.
- Rotation keeps the newest breaches of each process, so a renderer that
  breaches over and over never evicts the host's post-mortem. Earlier
  builds' renderer heap files are listed and rotated with their host
  breach, and a name no breach could have written is skipped.
- footprint's sections are bounded by their headers, so a header that
  names no pid credits no process and is said.
- The breach's words, the stats sentence and the warning come from one
  spelling. Approaching the limit is derived from the charge, never stored.
- The memory limit is a required input. capture-heap and the bench read
  every renderer's panel, and capture-heap uses the daemon's footprint
  parser.
- The stats reply is parsed where it arrives, as this build's snapshot or
  another build's skew.
- The design doc says what the backstop reads at one moment and what a
  named renderer's profile holds.

fix(host): an ended renderer is a phase of its own, and the stats reply asks only a renderer that can answer, within its budget (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.8xv)

- The supervisor's end is one transition into an ending phase: it serves no
  input, is judged no more, and its exit reports the reason the generation
  keeps. A second reason, or an end the phase refuses, is said. Only a hung
  renderer is ended from the close.
- A renderer is running, the state that carries its end and heap, only while
  live; one closing or ending is not running, with why.
- The stats reply does not ask a renderer that is not running, so a stats poll
  is no input it refused, and waits for any other at most half the
  connection's backstop, so one starting or busy renderer fails its own panel
  and not the reply.
- The stats skew check reads every renderer panel against one reference
  panel, down into the arm it answers with.

feat(host): each renderer process has its own memory backstop, and daemon-stats shows one panel per renderer

The backstop judged the host and its renderer as one sum, so one renderer's
leak would have ended the daemon and every session's bar. Each process is now
read at one moment and judged on its own charge. A renderer past the limit has
its memory report and heap snapshot written under an identity naming it, and
is ended through its supervisor, which starts it again as one that crashed;
every other renderer keeps drawing. The host past the limit ends the daemon as
before.

The stats reply carries the host's memory and one panel per renderer: where
its memory is (the host's process, no process and why, or its own process
against the limit), its mailbox, and what it answered of itself or why it gave
no answer. One down renderer fails only its own panel. The renderer-held
counts (render cache, effect cache, menu idle, turns, session state, frames
drawn) move from the top level onto the panels, and the restart forecast gives
way to each reading's near-limit flag.

A renderer the host has begun to end reads as not running, so a reading
between its end and its exit cannot breach it twice.

feat(bar-pane): pane gestures and hover, and a click mode for the statusline (#950)

* feat(bar-pane): an action answers more gestures, and the pane presses through a hit map of signed links

* feat(bar-pane): the pane that owns a session's pointer reports its gestures and hover, and the draw reads them as surface and hover

* feat(bar-pane): the statusline gets a click mode that reaches an action's hover and alt+click bindings, and the toggle stays live in every mode

* fix(bar-pane): review pass 1 — an action's gestures are walked everywhere, the pane survives one missed press, and the pointer's owner is derived from its followers

A gesture's target is an action reference every walker follows (unused, value reads, plugin names) through one list. The pane counts tmux's silence from the first miss of a run, exits on Ctrl-C, reads `mouse` from the list-panes call it already makes, sends one coalesced pointer report, and cuts its hit map to the lines it paints. The click mode is parsed once and derived once per draw. Recording export admits the pointer keys' modes. When the newest pane leaves, the one before it owns the pointer again.

* fix(bar-pane): the gesture tests import the helpers where main moved them

* fix(bar-pane): review pass 2 — a report made with no session followed no longer shuts the gate, the pointer is the pane that spoke last, and a side button runs nothing

* fix(bar-pane): review pass 3 — a pane reports only while the host holds its stream, a frame no pane follows is encoded once, and a missed press from long ago no longer counts against tmux

* fix(frame-feed): a failure building the pane's answer is the frame's, and the action-walk comment says which walks it covers

* test(bar-pane): the single-flight cases wait on microtasks, not the clock the unit tier refuses
